skill.name: Character from clues: actions, speech and how others react
skill.why: Writers rarely tell you what someone is like. They leave clues instead.
skill.how: Check what they do, what they say, and how others treat them.

steps.say: Indi here! Writers rarely say what someone is like. They leave clues. Clue one: what they do.

show.text: gave her last lolly to the new kid.

options.reason: A greedy kid keeps the lolly. What did Pip do with hers?
Pip didn't tell anyone what to do. Look at what she gave away.

steps.win: Yes! Giving away her last lolly shows Pip is kind. What a character does is a big clue.

steps.say: Clue two is what they say. Clue three is how other people react to them.

show.nudge: That's what Pip does. Look for what the other kids do.

show.text: 'You have the big one,' said Pip.
show.nudge: That's what Pip says. Look for what the other kids do.

show.text: The whole team cheered for Pip.

steps.ask: Tap how the other kids react to Pip.
steps.win: Yes! The team cheers for her. How others treat someone tells you what they're like.

steps.say: Pick the word that fits the clues exactly. Some words are close, but wrong.

show.text: She said no to every idea.

options.reason: Brave means doing something scary. Is anything scary here?
Careful people listen and check. Priya says no to every idea.

steps.win: Yes! She won't listen or change, even when it goes wrong. That's stubborn.

steps.say: Careful! What a character says about themselves can trick you.

show.text: 'I'm not scared of anything,' said Jett.
A twig snapped. Jett hid behind Mo.

options.reason: That's only his words. What does he do when the twig snaps?

options.text: all talk: his words don't match what he does
kind, because he stays near Mo
options.reason: He hides behind Mo. Is that kind, or scared?

steps.win: Yes! His words say brave, but his actions say scared. When they don't match, believe the actions.

steps.say: One clue on its own can trick you. The best word fits every clue.

show.text: Mrs Gruber scowled at the kids.
But she fixed Leni's bike for free.

steps.ask: Which word fits all the clues?

options.reason: That fits the scowl. But what did she do for Leni?
She fixed the bike, but she scowled. Does cheerful fit a scowl?

steps.win: Yes! The scowl and the free fix both fit. Check every clue before you pick.

terms.means: Their actions. What they choose to do is a big clue.
Their words. Check that their words match what they do.
How other characters treat them, like cheering, hiding or rolling their eyes.

examples.text: Everyone wanted Pip on their team.

card.test: Check what they do, say, and how others react. Pick the word that fits every clue.

weDo.text: Rocco found a wallet on the footpath. It had fifty dollars inside. 'Finders keepers!' said his cousin. 'No way,' said Rocco. 'Someone will be looking for this.' He walked it straight to the police station. The officer shook his hand.
weDo.hint: What does Rocco do with the money? What does he say about it?
weDo.success: Honest. He hands the wallet in and says someone will be looking for it.

options.reason: A greedy person would keep the fifty dollars. Rocco hands it in.
He walks the wallet all the way to the police station. That's not lazy.

weDo.prompt: Tap the clue that shows how the other kids react to Bree.
weDo.hint: Skip what Bree does and says. Look for what the other kids do.
weDo.success: Rolling their eyes and walking off shows the others are sick of Bree being bossy.

parts.tap: The other kids rolled their eyes and walked off.

creature.name: Sidlewink
creature.blurb: A pale ghost crab that never tells you what it's like. Watch what it does, listen to its clicks, and see how the gulls treat it.

encounters.frame: Narra the Teller is telling a story about the Twotide footy team. The Sidlewink is listening.
encounters.text: Jax was the fastest kid on the Twotide footy team. He knew it, too. 'I'm the best player here,' he told everyone before the game. 'You lot are lucky to have me.' When he kicked a goal, he ran to the crowd and bowed. When Kira kicked a goal, he said it was luck. At half-time, nobody wanted to sit next to Jax on the bench. He didn't notice. He was too busy telling the umpire about his goal.
encounters.prompt: What is Jax like?
encounters.success: A show-off. He brags, bows to the crowd and says Kira's goal was just luck.

options.reason: Shy people keep quiet. Jax tells everyone he's the best.
He says Kira's goal was luck. That isn't kind.

encounters.frame: Zed is telling the crew about the worst gamer he knows. The Sidlewink is taking notes.
encounters.text: Ollie and his big sister Dee played Kart Smash on the couch. The screen was split in half. Ollie kept looking at Dee's half. When she hid behind a tree, he knew right where she was. 'How do you keep finding me?' she asked. 'Skill,' said Ollie, with a grin. Then Mum walked in. 'Ollie, I can see you peeking,' she said. Dee put a cushion over her half of the screen. Ollie lost the next five games.
encounters.prompt: What is Ollie like?

options.reason: He says 'skill', but he was really peeking. That's not honest.

encounters.frame: The Sidlewink found a story about the spookiest house on Twotide Atoll.
encounters.text: Everyone said the house at the end of Shell Street was haunted. An old woman named Mrs Moss lived there. She wore a long black coat, even in summer. One day, Theo's ball flew over her fence. Mrs Moss came out holding it. 'You must be Theo,' she said. 'Come and get it any time.' Then she gave him a cupcake with a spider on top. It was a lolly spider. Now the kids wave to Mrs Moss every day.

encounters.frame: Narra the Teller is telling the crew about a drummer. The Sidlewink taps along.
encounters.text: Amira wanted to play the drums. She had no drum kit, so she made one. She used pots, pans and a bucket. She practised every afternoon after school. Her fingers got blisters. She put on plasters and kept going. 'That girl never gives up,' said her uncle. The dog next door howled along every day. After a year, Amira played at the school concert. That time, she used a real drum kit.
encounters.prompt: What is Amira like?
encounters.success: Determined. She practises every day, plays through blisters, and her uncle says she never gives up.

options.reason: She practises every afternoon, even with blisters. That's not lazy.
She never tells anyone what to do. She just keeps practising.

encounters.frame: Tully is telling the crew about her cousin's surf camp. The Sidlewink is drawing in the sand.
encounters.text: The Year 6 surf camp had two groups: the kids who could surf, and Benji. Benji fell off his board every single time. On the first morning, the best surfers waved Ari over. 'Come with us to the big waves,' said Tash. 'Leave Benji on the baby waves.' Ari looked at the big waves. Then he looked at Benji, who was spitting out seawater. 'Nah,' said Ari. 'Benji and I are a team.' He spent the whole day on the baby waves, pushing Benji onto every wave he could. By the afternoon, Benji stood up for three whole seconds. Ari cheered so loudly that a seagull dropped its chip. At dinner, Benji told everyone that Ari was the best mate in the world.
encounters.prompt: What is Ari like?
encounters.success: Loyal. He turns down the best surfers to stick with Benji, and Benji calls him the best mate.

options.reason: Nothing shows he's afraid of the big waves. He stays because 'Benji and I are a team.'
He gives up a day on the big waves to help Benji. That's the opposite of selfish.

encounters.frame: Indi heard about a mural that went wrong. The Sidlewink is pointing at two painters.
encounters.text: Rosa and Neve were painting a mural at the Twotide surf club. Rosa held the plan. 'You do the sky. You do the sand. Nobody touches the dolphins but me,' she said. When little Sam asked to help, Neve handed him her brush. She showed him how to paint fish. 'Just keep inside the lines,' she said gently. Rosa painted over Sam's fish because they were the wrong blue. Sam's lip wobbled. Neve helped him paint a bigger fish in the corner, and she wrote SAM next to it. When the mural was finished, Rosa told the newspaper she had done most of it. Sam drew Neve a picture of a fish wearing a crown.

encounters.success: Rosa gives orders and takes over. Neve shares and helps. Even Sam's picture is a clue.

encounters.frame: Mo is telling the crew about his favourite uncle. The Sidlewink keeps losing its place.
encounters.text: Uncle Dez was looking after the twins for the weekend. On Saturday morning, he poured orange juice on his cereal. He put his phone in the fridge and the butter in his pocket. He drove the twins to footy, then drove home without them. Halfway there, he turned around. 'Sorry, sorry!' he called out the window. At lunch, he searched the whole house for his glasses. They were on his head the whole time. 'Your uncle would forget his own birthday,' said Aunty Lou, shaking her head. 'He did, last year,' said one of the twins. That night, Uncle Dez read them a bedtime story. It was the same story as the night before. Neither twin said a thing. It was a good story.
encounters.prompt: What is Uncle Dez like?
encounters.success: Forgetful. Juice on his cereal, glasses on his head, and Aunty Lou says he'd forget his own birthday.

options.reason: He drives back for the twins and searches the whole house. Lazy people don't bother.
He says sorry and reads them a bedtime story. He just can't remember things.

encounters.frame: Gus is telling the crew about a slime disaster. The Sidlewink has slime on one claw.
encounters.text: Priya's slime would not set. It was still runny, like green soup. 'Add more glue,' said her brother. 'No,' said Priya. 'My recipe is perfect.' 'Maybe try the recipe on the box?' said Dad. 'My recipe is better than the box,' said Priya. She stirred it for an hour. It stayed runny. She stirred it for another hour. Dad put a towel under the bowl and quietly left the room. Her brother shook his head. 'She's been like this since she was two,' he said. At bedtime, the slime was still soup. Priya poured it into a jar and wrote a label: SLIME (NEARLY).
encounters.prompt: What is Priya like?
encounters.success: Stubborn. She refuses every idea, says her recipe is perfect, and her brother says she's always been like this.

options.reason: She stirs for two whole hours. That's not lazy.
Being careless isn't her problem. She won't listen to anyone else's idea.

encounters.frame: Zed has hacked into a Maxx Vantablack stream from the Echo Studio. The Sidlewink is watching with one eye.
encounters.text: 'Hey, Vantafam! Maxx here, saving baby turtles on Twotide Atoll!' Maxx flashed his huge white grin at the drone. 'These little guys are my whole life.' Behind him, a tiny hatchling was struggling towards the water. Maxx stepped right in front of it so the camera could get his good side. 'Smash that heart button like it owes you money!' When the drone flew off to film the sunset, Maxx's smile dropped. 'Ugh, sand in my runners,' he snapped. 'Someone fetch my gold towel.' A guard in a gold tracksuit sprinted over with it. Maxx didn't say thank you, and he didn't even look at him. The hatchling made it to the sea on its own. When the drone came back, Maxx was crouched by the water with a tear on his cheek. 'I did it, Vantafam,' he sniffed. 'I saved him.' Then he asked his followers to donate to the Maxx Rescue Fund, 'for the turtles'. Up on the dune, a ghost crab clicked its claws twice, which in crab means 'oh, please'.
encounters.prompt: What is Maxx really like?
encounters.success: Selfish and fake. He acts caring on camera, but blocks a hatchling for a shot and ignores his guard.

options.reason: That's only what he says to the camera. He steps right in front of a hatchling.

options.reason: He didn't forget. He didn't even look at the guard.

options.text: selfish, because he only acts caring for the camera

encounters.frame: Narra the Teller is telling a story about a school band. The Sidlewink is keeping the beat.
encounters.text: The Twotide Primary band had never won anything, and the competition started in ten minutes. The drummer had lost one stick, the trumpet player had hiccups, and the bass player was hiding in the toilets. Mei, who played the keyboard, didn't panic. She found a wooden spoon in the canteen and handed it to the drummer. 'Use this. Nobody will see it from the seats,' she said calmly. Then she knocked on the toilet door and talked to the bass player until he came out. 'We don't have to be perfect,' she told the whole band. 'We just have to start together.' The trumpet player gave her a thumbs up between hiccups. When the curtain opened, every single head in the band turned to Mei, waiting for her nod. She counted them in, and they started together. Halfway through the song, the trumpet player hiccupped right in the middle of his solo, so Mei simply played louder until he found his place again. They came fourth out of five, and the drummer kept the wooden spoon as a lucky charm.

encounters.text: Felix had never once admitted losing a game of Robo Brawl. When his little sister Maeve beat him on Saturday, he threw the controller onto the couch. encounters.frame: Narra the Teller is telling a story about the jetty. The Sidlewink has heard it a hundred times.
encounters.text: The kids of Twotide Atoll gave Old Bert's jetty a wide berth. He sat at the end of it every morning, a weathered man with a beard like a scrubbing brush, scowling at the water as though it owed him money. If anyone came too close, he grunted, 'Shove off, you'll scare the fish.' He even shouted at the pelicans, though he always seemed to have a tin of fish scraps for them in his bucket. Most of the kids did exactly that, and they told each other he had once thrown a boy into the sea for stepping on his line. Then, one stormy afternoon, eight-year-old Leni's tinny drifted loose from the boat ramp with her inside it. The adults were still running for the rescue boat when Old Bert was already in his dinghy, rowing hard through the chop. He towed her back, wrapped her in his own coat and said nothing at all, except, 'Next time, check your knots.' The following week, Leni found a neatly tied rope on her tinny and a small paper card showing six different knots, drawn in shaky pencil. Nobody saw Bert deliver it. He was back on his jetty, scowling at the fish, and when Leni waved, he grunted. But he didn't tell her to shove off.
encounters.prompt: Which description of Old Bert fits all the clues?
encounters.success: Gruff but caring. He grunts and scowls, but he rescues Leni and quietly teaches her knots.

options.text: cruel, as the kids say in their stories
options.reason: That's a rumour the kids tell. His actions, like the rescue and the knot card, show otherwise.

options.text: gruff on the outside but caring underneath

encounters.frame: Indi went to the Twotide Art Prize and wrote down what two artists said. The Sidlewink has mixed up the quotes.
encounters.text: The Twotide Art Prize is held every year in the old surf club, and this year's two finalists could hardly have been more different. Odette had painted a storm rolling over the lagoon in thick, swirling grey, and the judges had stood in front of it for ages without speaking. Ruben had painted himself, life-sized, in a gold frame he had built himself, with a small sign underneath that read MASTERPIECE (DO NOT TOUCH). When a reporter asked Odette about her painting, she shrugged and pointed at a picture of a kingfisher by a Year 3 student. 'Honestly, I think that one's better,' she said. 'Mine's still not quite finished.' Ruben didn't wait to be asked. He strode over and told the reporter that his painting was 'the best thing in the room, possibly in the country'. Then he turned to the photographer. 'Only shoot my left side, please,' he said. When Odette was announced as the winner, she went pink. 'Thank you to my art teacher, my mum and the lagoon,' she said. Ruben told everyone that the judges clearly didn't understand art. Then he wandered over to the prize table. 'Can I keep the ribbon, just to try it on?' he asked.

encounters.frame: Wren found a page from a Mars base newsletter in a bottle on the beach. The Sidlewink is reading over her shoulder.
encounters.text: Red Hollow Base sat under a glass dome on the edge of a crater, and only forty families lived there, so a new kid was big news. When Tova arrived at Red Hollow Base, the other kids decided within a day that she was rude. She ate lunch alone at the end of the long table, staring at her tray. When Kip asked where she was from, she said 'Earth' and nothing else, which, as Kip complained afterwards, was where everybody was from. In class, she never put her hand up, and when the teacher called on her, her voice came out so quietly that nobody could hear. Then small things began appearing around the base. Someone fixed the wobbly wheel on Kip's moon-buggy model overnight. Someone left a perfectly drawn map of the air vents in the games room, with the best hiding spots marked in red. When the twins' pet beetle escaped, someone found it and left it in a jar outside their door, with a lettuce leaf and a note that said 'He was in the laundry'. The handwriting matched the labels on Tova's locker. When Kip finally thanked her, she turned bright pink, stared at her boots and mumbled, 'It was nothing.' The next day, she sat in the middle of the table.
encounters.prompt: Which description of Tova fits all the clues?
encounters.success: Shy but kind. She's too quiet to talk much, but she secretly helps everyone, then blushes when thanked.

encounters.frame: Mo wrote a note about his Aunty Pam for the crew. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: Aunty Pam believes everything she sees on a screen. Last month, a video told her that eating twelve bananas a day would let her see in the dark, so she ate twelve bananas a day for a week and walked into the clothesline every night. When an email promised that she had won a castle in Scotland, she packed a suitcase and bought a tartan hat. When a fortune cookie told her she would meet a tall stranger, she spent a whole afternoon waiting at the ferry terminal with a welcome sign. 'Pam, that's not real,' her brother says at least once a week. 'It might be,' she always replies. Now she watches Maxx Vantablack's stream every single evening. 'Maxx rescues three Creatures before breakfast,' she told the family at dinner, her eyes shining. 'He said so himself.' Mo's cousin Lily showed her a photo of a Creature in a tiny gold cage behind Maxx's studio. Aunty Pam studied it for a long time. 'That's probably a rescue cage,' she decided. 'For their safety.' That night, she spent ninety dollars on an official MaxxCam rescue whistle, which came in a gold box and turned out to be a party blower. The family has started a group chat called Before Pam Buys It, where they check things first.

encounters.frame: Gus is reading a news report out loud, very crossly. The Sidlewink is hiding from the smell.
encounters.text: TWOTIDE TIMES. A twelve-year-old scientist has won the Island Science Medal for inventing a spray that turns rotting seaweed into garden fertiliser. 'It was all my idea,' said Dorian Finch, holding up the medal. 'I'm basically a genius.' However, the report on his project tells a different story. The spray, which neighbours say smells 'like a wet dog that ate a dead fish', has already been sold to three local farms. The spray was mixed by his lab partner, Ruby Ngata, who spent six weeks testing it on buckets of stinking kelp. At the awards night, Dorian gave a twenty-minute speech that did not mention Ruby once. When the reporter asked Ruby what she thought, she simply raised one eyebrow and kept cleaning test tubes. Their science teacher, Mr Abara, gave a careful smile. 'Dorian is very good at presentations,' he said. 'Ruby is very good at science.' When asked about Ruby, Dorian said he had 'forgotten' to put her name on the entry form, then added that she had mostly 'held the buckets'. Ruby's notebook, which has two hundred pages of results, says otherwise. The medal committee has announced it will be reviewing the entry next week, and Mr Abara has offered Ruby a seat on the panel.
encounters.prompt: What do the clues show about Dorian?
encounters.success: He takes credit for Ruby's work. Ruby's eyebrow, Mr Abara's careful words and the notebook all show it.

options.text: He is brilliant, because he won the medal.
options.reason: The medal was for work Ruby mostly did. The clues show the win isn't really his.

options.text: He is forgetful, because he forgot Ruby's name on the form.
options.reason: The report puts 'forgotten' in quotation marks. Nobody believes he really forgot.

He is hard-working, because the project took six weeks.
options.reason: Ruby did the six weeks of testing. Her notebook shows the work was hers.
